summary: Gendron, Rožanec, Witbrock, and Dobbie propose an end-to-end LLM method for extracting causal variables and graphs from text, merging across sources, and performing counterfactual inference via conditional LLM interventions. They state LLM counterfactual limitations stem from prediction errors.
limitations:
The source authors state: "6

Limitations

LLMs provide free-text answers that can be different from the format provided in the instructions."
abstract: The paper proposes a framework for causal structure discovery and evaluation from natural language text using LLMs, dividing work into extraction, summarisation, counterfactual queries, and graph evaluation stages.
introduction: Gendron, Rožanec, Witbrock, and Dobbie propose an end-to-end method for causal structure discovery and counterfactual inference from natural language text using LLMs.
conclusion: The authors state that LLM limitations in counterfactual causal reasoning come from prediction errors.
